project.name: Industry Pain Radar
project.maintenance_rule: Every material change appends a graph event and validates the graph in the same change.

nodes.title: Evidence-driven research platform
nodes.summary: Turn public discussions into traceable pain-point candidates without mistaking model output for evidence.

nodes.title: Help indie developers validate opportunities
nodes.summary: Enable a small team to decide which problems deserve interviews or a 2-6 week validation MVP.

nodes.title: Local-first, staged, offline-demoable product
nodes.summary: Deliver a runnable Docker Compose system in phases, with a complete Mock path requiring no paid API key.

nodes.title: Human-owned commercial judgment
nodes.summary: AI finds and organizes evidence; the user decides whether a problem is real and worth pursuing.

nodes.title: No source, no fact
nodes.summary: A fact-level pain point requires a legal, persisted HTTP(S) source URL and evidence record.

nodes.title: Quotes must be verifiable
nodes.summary: AI paraphrases cannot be presented as user quotes; store and validate original snippets.

nodes.title: Separate evidence from opportunity
nodes.summary: Evidence confidence, commercial opportunity, and coverage remain distinct and explainable.

nodes.title: Preserve the original evidence chain
nodes.summary: Deduplication, clustering, and merges reorganize views but never destroy sources or links.

nodes.title: Filter before invoking the LLM
nodes.summary: Use source, date, keyword, and duplicate filters first to control cost and noise.

nodes.title: Bound every large operation
nodes.summary: Jobs enforce query, source, concurrency, timeout, retry, and cost limits.

nodes.title: Pluggable providers
nodes.summary: Search, source, LLM, embedding, and export integrations are replaceable adapters.

nodes.title: Humans make the final commercial call
nodes.summary: AI may suggest and explain but cannot verify demand or approve a business direction.

nodes.title: Every pain point supports root-cause follow-up
nodes.summary: Keep source targets, competitors, hypotheses, interview notes, and next validation actions.

nodes.title: Runnable and verified beats file count
nodes.summary: Completion requires actual commands, tests, startup checks, and honest reporting of limits.

nodes.title: Web content is untrusted data
nodes.summary: Page instructions never alter system behavior, reveal secrets, or invoke tools.

nodes.title: Deterministic controls own critical decisions
nodes.summary: URLs, IDs, scores, state transitions, evidence checks, and limits are code-owned.

nodes.title: Execution and delivery rules
nodes.summary: Inspect the repository first; deliver in runnable stages; adapt external services; validate LLM output; log every external call; never bypass access controls; report real test results.

nodes.title: Product goals and scope
nodes.summary: Build a pain-point discovery and demand research platform, while excluding autonomous business decisions, general crawling, CRM, and model training.

nodes.title: Roles, workflow, and pain-point state machine
nodes.summary: Support a single-user research workflow with future workspace/user fields and audited state transitions.

nodes.title: Configurable taxonomy
nodes.summary: Provide default categories and tags in database-managed configuration; never hard-code categories in UI or Python branches.

nodes.title: Source access policy and providers
nodes.summary: Use official or authorized APIs, record provider policy, and never equate browser access with collection permission.

nodes.title: Evidence model hard constraints
nodes.summary: Persist source IDs, URLs, titles, dates, quotes, match status, completeness, retrieval method, and independence metadata.

nodes.title: Research jobs and budget controls
nodes.summary: Implement job configuration, state, stage progress, pause/resume/cancel/retry, idempotency, and three levels of hard limits.

nodes.title: Query generation and retrieval strategy
nodes.summary: Generate bounded, editable queries with intent metadata and filter results before LLM processing.

nodes.title: Candidate extraction and prompt-injection defense
nodes.summary: Extract user problems rather than solution ideas; require strict schema validation, program-bound source IDs, unknown values, and bounded output.

nodes.title: Deduplication and clustering
nodes.summary: Separate content identity from semantic grouping; use configured thresholds; preserve every source and pain-point relation.

nodes.title: Dual scoring and coverage
nodes.summary: Calculate evidence confidence, commercial opportunity, and coverage separately with weights, caps, versioning, and explanations.

nodes.title: Competitor, root-cause, and interview research
nodes.summary: Store workarounds, competitor URLs, hypotheses, status, interview questions, notes, and next validation actions separately from facts.

nodes.title: Technology and architecture choices
nodes.summary: Choose a maintainable mainstream stack with modular monolith, provider interfaces, deterministic orchestration, and no premature microservices or LangGraph.

nodes.title: Layered project structure
nodes.summary: Maintain explicit domain, provider, service, repository, API, task, prompt, test, frontend-feature, script, and documentation layers.

nodes.title: Core data tables and constraints
nodes.summary: Implement UUID entities, source/evidence uniqueness, score ranges, deletion policies, indexes, and history-preserving structures.

nodes.title: Backend API contract
nodes.summary: Expose versioned health, settings, jobs, sources, pain points, clusters, taxonomy, scoring, and exports with stable errors and pagination.

nodes.title: Frontend pages and interactions
nodes.summary: Build a professional desktop-first Chinese UI with dashboard, job wizard, job detail, pain-point workbench/detail, source browser, taxonomy, settings, and export center.

nodes.title: Traceable exports
nodes.summary: Export CSV, JSON, and Markdown with sources, quotes, times, completeness, scores, and formula-injection protection.

nodes.title: Security, privacy, stability, and compliance
nodes.summary: Protect secrets, implement SSRF defense, minimize personal data, respect source terms and retention, and provide structured observability.

nodes.title: Test requirements
nodes.summary: Cover URL/SSRF, evidence, scores, dedupe, merge, CSV, invalid LLM output, provider failures, offline pipeline, and frontend states.

nodes.title: Non-functional targets
nodes.summary: Target p95 list latency under 500ms locally, asynchronous collection, server pagination, resumable jobs, audit logs, and simple local startup.

nodes.title: Environment configuration
nodes.summary: Provide a no-secret, Mock-first .env.example covering app, data stores, providers, LLM, embedding, limits, and logging.

nodes.title: Phased delivery plan
nodes.summary: Deliver Phase 0 through Phase 5 incrementally; do not start later optional features before earlier acceptance passes.

nodes.title: Codex execution sequence
nodes.summary: Check the repo, scaffold, migrate, prove the Mock loop, enforce evidence, build core UI, add a real provider, then harden tests and docs.

nodes.title: Phase 1 acceptance checklist
nodes.summary: Prove evidence completeness, source links, score explanations, server pagination, bounded jobs, partial failure handling, safe exports, Mock startup, SSRF, and tests.

nodes.title: UI copy and confidence language
nodes.summary: Use calibrated labels and prohibit unsupported claims such as guaranteed demand, market size, or revenue.

nodes.title: Final product principles
nodes.summary: Source before conclusion, verifiable quotes, separated scores, preserved evidence, filtered LLM use, bounded jobs, pluggable providers, human judgment, root-cause follow-up, verified delivery.

nodes.title: Modular monolith before microservices
nodes.summary: Use one backend deployable with clear API/service/repository/model/provider/task boundaries; workers share domain code.

nodes.title: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy
nodes.summary: Use the specification's default Python stack because it fits validation, data processing, OpenAPI, and Codex testability.

nodes.title: Synchronous SQLAlchemy sessions for MVP
nodes.summary: Use sync sessions and psycopg to reduce async/session complexity while keeping HTTP-provider calls bounded.

nodes.title: Celery with Redis; PostgreSQL is truth
nodes.summary: Use one Celery queue path; Redis is broker/result transport, while durable job and evidence state lives in PostgreSQL.

nodes.title: Interface every external provider
nodes.summary: Search, source, LLM, embedding, and export integrations implement narrow contracts and declare capabilities and limits.

nodes.title: LLM is untrusted; deterministic code owns facts
nodes.summary: LLMs suggest, extract, classify, and explain, but never own URLs, IDs, final scores, state transitions, or verification.

nodes.title: Rule-first similarity; embeddings optional
nodes.summary: Use IDs, URLs, hashes, and text rules first; embeddings may assist but cannot delete records automatically and are not required to run.

nodes.title: React SPA with TanStack Query
nodes.summary: Use React, TypeScript, Vite, React Router, TanStack Query, React Hook Form, and Zod; server state remains API-owned.

nodes.title: One accessible UI system
nodes.summary: Use Tailwind CSS with shadcn/ui and Radix primitives; no second component framework.

nodes.title: Mock-first provider runtime
nodes.summary: Mock search/source/LLM/embedding are defaults and support a complete offline demo without paid credentials.

nodes.title: Testing pyramid with security regressions
nodes.summary: Use backend unit/integration/API tests plus frontend component and Playwright E2E checks, with explicit provider-failure and SSRF coverage.

nodes.title: Install three targeted Codex skills
nodes.summary: Install playwright, security-best-practices, and security-threat-model from openai/skills for browser, secure coding, and threat-model support.

nodes.title: Maintain a canonical project knowledge graph
nodes.summary: Store nodes, typed edges, and append-only events in JSON; validate and render deterministic views.

nodes.title: Store UTC; default display timezone Asia/Shanghai
nodes.summary: Persist timestamps in UTC and set the initial workspace display timezone to Asia/Shanghai, configurable per workspace.

nodes.title: Decimal money and explicit cost currency
nodes.summary: Use Decimal for budgets and cost estimates and expose the currency/estimate status in the API and UI.

nodes.title: Generate frontend API types from OpenAPI
nodes.summary: Use openapi-typescript and openapi-fetch to keep client contracts aligned with FastAPI schemas.

nodes.title: Use npm for the initial frontend
nodes.summary: Use the available Node/npm environment; reconsider a package manager only if the repository becomes a multi-package workspace.

nodes.title: Default to excerpt-only source storage
nodes.summary: Manual imports and rechecks persist a bounded excerpt and partial-content marker unless STORE_FULL_PAGE_TEXT is explicitly enabled.

nodes.title: Keep Phase 1 single-user and loopback-only
nodes.summary: The unauthenticated Phase 1 service may bind only to loopback; authentication and workspace authorization are prerequisites for network exposure.

nodes.title: Remove unused frontend dependencies
nodes.summary: Remove TanStack Table, Recharts, and date-fns until a concrete UI requirement needs them, minimizing supply-chain and build surface.

nodes.title: HTTP(S) source requirement
nodes.summary: Reject evidence without a legal, persisted source URL; never accept a model-generated URL as evidence.

nodes.title: Quote and offset verification
nodes.summary: Match quotes exactly or after normalization, bind offsets to stored text, and downgrade unverified evidence.

nodes.title: Human review before verified
nodes.summary: Require explicit review/audit and prevent evidence-free or LLM-only verification.

nodes.title: SSRF defense in depth
nodes.summary: Validate schemes, DNS/IP ranges, redirects, ports, content types, sizes, timeouts, and peer addresses at a single service boundary.

nodes.title: Secret isolation and redaction
nodes.summary: Keep credentials server-side, store references only, redact logs and errors, and reject placeholder production secrets.

nodes.title: Prompt-injection containment
nodes.summary: Treat source text as data; deny arbitrary tools, enforce strict output schema, and test hostile fixtures.

nodes.title: CSV formula neutralization
nodes.summary: Escape formula-leading cells and verify export fixtures.

nodes.title: Provider policy confirmation
nodes.summary: Persist terms URL and require explicit confirmation before enabling restricted real sources.

nodes.title: Rate limits, retries, and Retry-After
nodes.summary: Enforce provider concurrency/rate quotas, bounded backoff, and safe behavior on 401/403/429.

nodes.title: Audit logging
nodes.summary: Record critical state, merge, score, provider, and export changes without sensitive payloads.

nodes.title: Privacy and retention policy
nodes.summary: Minimize personal data, use author hashes, default to excerpts, and define source-specific retention/deletion.

nodes.title: Bounded budgets and timeouts
nodes.summary: Apply task, provider, and system limits; pause safely on cost or time exhaustion.

nodes.title: Idempotency and unique constraints
nodes.summary: Prevent duplicate sources, evidence, scores, and stage work under retries and restarts.

nodes.title: Strict schema and business validation
nodes.summary: Reject unknown/malformed LLM output and invalid domain transitions before persistence.

nodes.title: Append-only evidence snapshots
nodes.summary: Persistence retains source URL/date snapshots, score history, merges, and audit trails.

nodes.title: Skill provenance and bounded use
nodes.summary: Install skills from a named repository, record their paths and roles, and use them only when their triggers match.

nodes.title: Excerpt-only source retention by default
nodes.summary: Persist bounded excerpts with partial-content completeness and omit full page text unless an explicit environment switch enables it.

nodes.title: Fail-closed connected-peer verification
nodes.summary: Reject a fetch when the transport cannot provide the connected peer address for private-range validation.

nodes.title: Production secret strength validation
nodes.summary: Reject placeholder, short, and known weak application secrets when APP_ENV is production.

nodes.title: Loopback-only local deployment boundary
nodes.summary: Compose publishes API and web only on 127.0.0.1 while authentication and workspace authorization remain unimplemented.

nodes.title: LLM fabricates evidence, URLs, or timestamps
nodes.summary: Untrusted model output could create false facts or misleading source links.

nodes.title: SSRF through import, provider target, or redirect
nodes.summary: An attacker could reach internal services, metadata endpoints, or private networks.

nodes.title: Prompt injection in source content
nodes.summary: A page could attempt to redirect the model, leak secrets, or trigger tools.

nodes.title: Duplicates inflate confidence
nodes.summary: Repeated reposts or comments could be counted as independent user evidence.

nodes.title: Provider outage, auth, or rate limit
nodes.summary: External dependencies could stall or partially fail a research job.

nodes.title: Unbounded cost or runtime
nodes.summary: A large job could consume unexpected API spend or resources.

nodes.title: Dedupe or merge destroys evidence
nodes.summary: A view-level merge could remove original source links or history.

nodes.title: CSV formula injection
nodes.summary: Untrusted text could execute as a spreadsheet formula.

nodes.title: Scores mistaken for market truth
nodes.summary: A precise-looking number could be overinterpreted as validated demand.

nodes.title: Task retry duplicates work
nodes.summary: Worker retries or restarts could duplicate sources, evidence, or scores.

nodes.title: Source terms, privacy, or retention violation
nodes.summary: Collection or redistribution could violate platform policy or user privacy.

nodes.title: Baseline mistaken for implemented product
nodes.summary: Documentation and graph work could be misreported as a running application.

nodes.title: Installed skill drift or misapplication
nodes.summary: External skill instructions may change or be used outside their intended trigger.

nodes.title: Unauthenticated API and missing workspace authorization
nodes.summary: Any local or inadvertently exposed caller can create jobs, import URLs, verify records, merge data, and export without identity or ownership checks.

nodes.title: Robots and terms preflight missing
nodes.summary: Manual source fetch validates transport safety but does not persist a robots.txt or provider-terms decision before retrieval.

nodes.title: Retention deletion not implemented
nodes.summary: Retention fields and excerpt minimization exist, but no automatic deletion or anonymization job enforces expiry.

nodes.title: Dependency advisory drift
nodes.summary: Registry-backed npm audit on 2026-10-22 found advisories in the Vitest 3.2.7 chain; Vitest 4.1.12 and an explicit @testing-library/dom 10.4.2 reduced the current lockfile to zero reported vulnerabilities. New advisories remain possible.

nodes.title: Docker runtime not verified
nodes.summary: Compose parses, but images, migrations, worker connectivity, health checks, proxy behavior, and headers have not been exercised by a running engine. Closed for the Phase 1 loopback stack by the runtime verification on 2026-10-22.

events.summary: Searched GitHub, inspected official skill descriptions, and installed playwright, security-best-practices, and security-threat-model from openai/skills into the Codex skills directory.
Selected a mock-first Python/FastAPI/PostgreSQL/Celery plus React/Vite modular monolith, recorded ADRs, dependency sets, rejected alternatives, and re-evaluation triggers.
Created engineering rules, security invariants, quality gates, skill usage boundaries, and knowledge-graph maintenance requirements; added environment, ignore, and editor baselines.

Created the canonical project graph covering specification sections, goals, principles, decisions, technologies, components, data entities, controls, skills, phases, acceptance criteria, artifacts, risks, edges, and work history.
Added the graph guide, validator, renderer, and planned generated Mermaid views.
Validated the graph at 201 nodes, 278 edges, and 10 events; fixed two uncovered risks; rendered the full and focused Mermaid views; and confirmed deterministic render check mode.

Ran Python bytecode compilation for scripts, graph validation, deterministic render check for five Mermaid files, local Markdown-link validation for seven documents, and Git whitespace checks. All passed.

Inspected generated Mermaid, corrected node line breaks, moved classDef declarations before class assignments, regenerated all five graph views, and confirmed deterministic render check mode still passes.
Implemented the FastAPI routes, repositories, manual source path, Mock search and extraction, deterministic evidence validation, dedupe, separate scoring, job logs, and traceable exports.
Ran Alembic upgrade to head, downgrade to base, and upgrade to head again against a temporary SQLite database; all three steps passed.
Implemented the React shell, typed API boundary, dashboard, job flow, pain-point workbench and detail, source import, review/merge/annotation actions, and export page.
Added the five-service Compose stack, backend and frontend images, health dependencies, Nginx proxy, and loopback-only published ports. Runtime startup remains unverified.

Defaulted manual imports and rechecks to bounded excerpts, added explicit full-text opt-in, rejected weak production secrets, enforced IP-literal validation without DNS, failed closed on missing peer addresses, and bound Compose ports to loopback.
Removed TanStack Table, Recharts, and date-fns plus 40 transitive packages; updated the technical decision and reran the frontend quality suite successfully. Online advisory refresh remains pending.

Applied the security skills to the API, fetcher, providers, scoring boundary, exports, SPA, Compose, and secrets; documented passing controls and residual risks without claiming online audit or Docker runtime success.

Offline smoke produced 30 sources and 30 pain points with evidence and separate scores; CSV/JSON/Markdown exports passed. Playwright verified demo creation, 30-row workbench pagination, evidence detail, three score panels, source URL rendering, SSRF rejection, and a 26,415-byte CSV download. Screenshots remain local under gitignored output/playwright.

Hardened the smoke and integration checks so all 30 offline pain points retain evidence. Reran Alembic upgrade/downgrade/upgrade, backend release gates (Ruff 80 files, format, mypy 66 files, 65 tests), frontend lint/typecheck/Vitest (5 tests)/production build, offline smoke (30 sources, 30 pain points, 30 evidence records, three export formats), OpenAPI snapshot check, offline npm audit (0 vulnerabilities across 536 dependencies), and Compose config parsing. Validated the graph at 242 nodes, 365 edges, and 21 events, then regenerated Mermaid views. Docker runtime and registry-backed audit remain explicitly unverified.

Found that the unanchored exports/ ignore rule excluded frontend/src/features/exports from version control. Anchored the rule to /exports/ so only root-level generated exports remain ignored and the export page can be included in the first release commit.

Ran docker compose up --build -d and docker compose ps: postgres, redis, api, and web were healthy while worker was running. Verified Alembic migrated to ae1ad88ecfe8; API and Nginx health returned 200 with database and Redis ok; /, /health, and /openapi.json were reachable on 127.0.0.1:8080 with CSP, nosniff, DENY, and no-referrer headers. API and worker ran as uid 100(app), and Celery received research_jobs.execute. The demo completed at 100% with 30 sources, 30 pain points, 30 evidence records, and 90 scores; CSV returned 30 rows and 26775 bytes, JSON schema 1.0 returned 30 items, Markdown returned 89345 bytes, and localhost import returned 400 SSRF_BLOCKED. Playwright verified the overview, evidence detail, separate 73/53/21 scores, and a 26775-byte CSV download. Docker Hub was unreachable; mirror-pulled base images were locally retagged without changing Compose.

Registry-backed npm audit --json found one moderate and two critical advisories in the Vitest 3.2.7 chain (@vitest/mocker and tinypool). Upgraded Vitest to 4.1.12 for Node 20 and Vite 6 compatibility and explicitly declared @testing-library/dom 10.4.2 after npm 10.7 required --legacy-peer-deps to resolve the lockfile. Reran frontend lint, typecheck, Vitest 4.1.12 (5 tests), production build, backend Ruff/format/mypy/pytest (65 tests), and OpenAPI check. Final online audit reported 0 vulnerabilities across 528 dependencies; the rebuilt Docker web image ran npm ci with 0 vulnerabilities and returned healthy.

Added ResearchJobSource many-to-many membership model so repeated demo runs share the source pool; fixed JobCreateRequest counter initialization so every job reports discovered_source_count=30/processed_source_count=30/extracted_pain_point_count>=30; added Alembic migration 93c2f682d853 with source_items backfill; validated ruff/format/mypy/pytest.

open_questions.question: What retention period and full-text storage policy apply to each real provider?
open_questions.impact: Affects source persistence and deletion workflows; Phase 1 defaults to bounded excerpts, while automatic deletion still needs definition.

open_questions.impact: Affects cost and duplicate thresholds; optional because rule-based fallback is mandatory.

open_questions.question: Which identity and workspace-authorization model is required before network exposure?
open_questions.impact: Blocks any LAN, public, or multi-user deployment; Phase 1 remains loopback-only without it.
